description: Dependency DAG of the Proximity Prize program. Nodes = statements/artifacts/experiments; edges point FROM a dependency TO the statement it supports. gate=all: every 'req' child needed; gate=any: one 'alt' child suffices (plus all 'req'). Statuses: PROVED (on main w/ proof or exact verification), PROVABLE (route pinned, write-up pending), CONDITIONAL (proved under stated hypothesis), CONJECTURE (precise statement, unproved), TARGET (fuzzy, expected to sharpen), WALL (frozen hard core w/ consumer theorem), REFUTED (dead route), TEST (experiment/prediction). Source of truth for statuses: experimental/notes/roadmaps/ (r2 + proof_sketch + wp_detail). REFINEMENT PRINCIPLES (2026-07-02): (1) critical nodes carry exact 'statement' fields (+ attack_surface/falsifier notes) — machine-enforced; (2) new conjectured nodes are admitted ONLY as branches of exhaustive splits, proved equivalences/reductions, or with a named non-ev consumer + truth-confidence note — never as speculative lemma chains presuming a proof shape; (3) every critical conjecture gets a cheap wired falsifier TEST.

nodes.statement: Bezout-type bounds: the alignment variety X_{u,v} and its intersections with structure loci have an explicitly bounded number of irreducible components with bounded degrees (explicit in n, t, j). The component LIST is the finite enumeration.

nodes.title: SPI stage 2: points of D_j on components — low-dim components contribute poly
nodes.statement: For each component V of dim below threshold: #(V cap D_j) <= poly(n). HONEST NOTE: this is where the core resurfaces in the SPI dialect — D_j is a special finite set, not generic points, so Lang-Weil-type counting does not apply verbatim; the divisor structure must enter.

nodes.title: ES route: adapt the algebraic regularity lemma (Tao) as the off-the-shelf enumerator
nodes.statement: Formulate alignment as a definable relation of bounded description complexity and apply an F_q algebraic-regularity/ES-type theorem: structure-vs-pseudorandomness with power savings, exceptional sets ALGEBRAIC and classifiable. Named obstacle: bounded complexity vs our degrees growing with t — the same dimension-free obstacle in regularity-lemma clothing.

nodes.title: Monodromy route stage 0: realize general aperiodic alignment as sheaf monodromy
nodes.statement: Express the aperiodic alignment count (general pairs, in-band agreements) as the trace function of an explicit sheaf family, so that big-monodromy + subgroup classification (the BETA_2 machinery, worked for the slack-line instance) applies. The enumeration = the subgroup classification (Kantor/ADW-style), complete by group theory.
nodes.notes: the unmapped step: BETA_2's sheaf covers ONE instance; the general realization is open

nodes.title: PMA stage 1: mixed-petal extras = RS list of the auxiliary pieced word (one level down)
nodes.statement: Fix defect set D (|D| = d) and background R_P. Non-planted extras inject (P -> W_P, proved unique) into the list of degree-<=d polynomials agreeing with the auxiliary word U*(x) = c_i L_D(x) on T_i (well-defined: petals disjoint) at agreement N = d+1+sigma-|R_P|, with W = 0 on R_P. The D-choice entropy C(k-1,d) is charged to the reserve — the same budget line as all locator combinatorics.
nodes.notes: elementary from the PROVED core-defect lemma; turns the amplification problem into list decoding at degree d

nodes.title: PMA stage 2: few-petal regime is CLASSICAL — Johnson/GS list bound applies
nodes.statement: Whenever N^2 > d |T| (T = union of petals, |T| = M(sigma+1)), i.e. petal count M below ~(d+sigma)^2/(d(sigma+1)), the per-D auxiliary list is poly by Guruswami-Sudan — an unconditional classical import (forward direction; bridge-ledger row).

nodes.title: PMA stage 3 (the residue): many-petal, sub-Johnson regime with CORRELATED targets
nodes.statement: For M above the Johnson threshold: bound the auxiliary list despite sub-Johnson agreement. The structure not yet exploited: all petal targets c_i L_D come from ONE polynomial L_D (the word is far from arbitrary), the per-petal cap |S_i| <= d spreads agreement thin, and W vanishes on R_P.
nodes.attack_surface: two independent angles: (a) correlated-target strengthening of GS (the c_i are scalars times a COMMON L_D — one-dimensional target space per petal); (b) descent: extras of the auxiliary problem are degree-d objects — the SAME problem at (k, sigma) -> (d+1, ...), strictly smaller; iterate until Johnson-safe. Q2.9 fixed-excess data calibrates both.
nodes.falsifier: an adversarial many-petal family (R3 attack) with super-poly auxiliary list
